#Specialized_Viewpoint 794 #Regulation

🔰 The National Artificial Intelligence Development Law: Iran's Entry Point into Regulation or the Trap of Premature Rules

👤 Amirhossein Zanbaq, a researcher in the Regulation Group at the Sharif Governance Think Tank, has written in a note:

🔹The experience of the European AI Act shows that strict regulation, even with high institutional capacity, has run into delays and implementation difficulties. Iran cannot copy the European model, because the main issue is still the formation of the industry, not the control of a mature industry.

🔸The following three key proposals can serve as a starting point for regulation:

▫️The principle should be to facilitate development and regulate in proportion to risk, not to require prior licensing for all applications. Low-risk applications should be governed through ex-post oversight and general rules, and only high-risk applications should be subject to greater oversight.

▫️The National Artificial Intelligence Organization should play the role of coordinator, not serve as the detailed regulator of all sectors. Common national principles should be established, and the details should be left to the regulators of each sector.

▫️Regulation should be accompanied by market development tools.

From the development plans before the revolution to the five-year plans after the revolution, the government has written development plans, implemented development projects, invested in industry and infrastructure, and was supposed to direct the country's resources toward increasing production capacity and long-term development. 🔸But a developmentalist government is not just a government that builds projects or writes development plans. #Specialized_View 788#Parliament_Studies🔰The Necessity of Recognizing the Government👤Hadith Rabiei, Director of the Parliament Studies Group at the think tank, wrote in a note on the occasion of Government Week in Farhikhtegan:🔹Governments need authority, coordination, and executive power to solve public issues; but this authority is effective only when other components of the political structure also accept the government as the main and responsible actor. 🔸A government that is not sufficiently recognized within the power structure will find it harder to establish its authority in society; and a government that lacks symbolic authority and organized communication in society becomes more vulnerable within the power structure as well. These two weaknesses reinforce each other and create a vicious cycle: the weakening of institutional authority reduces implementation capacity; reduced implementation capacity creates social dissatisfaction; social dissatisfaction erodes the government's credibility.📌Read the full text on the think tank's website.🗞️ Published in: Farhikhtegan💠 Sharif Governance Think Tank |Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|
